title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals Video Calendar — Session Date and Notice Period
content:
The video session notice period under Unemployment Insurance Appeals is the number of calendar days from today, the day the party books the session and its notice is mailed, to the video session date. The video session date is the set hearing date moved later by the video block gap. The video block gap is the standard video block days, **5** calendar days. A video session date that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday moves to the following Monday.

## How the figure is reached

1. **Set hearing date.** The hearing date currently set on the appeal record. Its distance from today, in calendar days, is the starting count.
2. **Video block gap.** The set hearing date is moved 5 calendar days later; the date reached is the date found.
3. **Weekend.** A date found on a Saturday moves 2 days, and one on a Sunday 1 day, to the following Monday; any other weekday stands.
4. **Notice period.** The calendar days from today (day 0) to the date from point 3 — equivalently, the total of the days from today to the set hearing date, the block gap and any weekend move.

Every count is in calendar days.

## Worked computations (hypothetical inputs; today is Wednesday 15 April 2026)

| Set hearing date | Date found (5 days later) | Weekend move | Video session date | Notice period |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monday 4 May 2026 | Saturday 9 May | 2 days | Monday 11 May | 26 days |
| Tuesday 28 April 2026 | Sunday 3 May | 1 day | Monday 4 May | 19 days |
| Thursday 30 April 2026 | Tuesday 5 May | none | Tuesday 5 May | 20 days |

In the first row: the set hearing date is 19 days after today; the block gap adds 5, giving 24 days (Saturday 9 May); the weekend move adds 2, giving a notice period of 26 days.
